- This function should convert C standard datetime format codes to regex patterns.
- Common codes: %Y (4-digit year), %m (month 01-12), %d (day 01-31), %H (hour 00-23), %M (minute 00-59), %S (second 00-59), %f (microseconds), %z (timezone), etc.

Let me think about what a proper implementation would look like:

```python
def dt_format_to_regex(format):
    """Convert C standard datetime format codes to regex patterns."""
    # Map of format codes to regex patterns
    CODE_MAP = {
        '%Y': r'\d{4}',      # Year with century
        '%y': r'\d{2}',      # Year without century
        '%m': r'\d{1,2}',    # Month (01-12)
        '%d': r'\d{1,2}',    # Day (01-31)
        '%H': r'\d{1,2}',    # Hour (00-23)
        '%I': r'\d{1,2}',    # Hour (01-12)
        '%M': r'\d{1,2}',    # Minute (00-59)
        '%S': r'\d{1,2}',    # Second (00-59)
        '%f': r'\d+',        # Microseconds
        '%z': r'[+-]\d{2}:?\d{2}',  # UTC offset
        '%Z': r'[A-Za-z]+',  # Timezone name
        '%a': r'[A-Za-z]+',  # Abbreviated weekday
        '%A': r'[A-Za-z]+',  # Full weekday
        '%b': r'[A-Za-z]+',  # Abbreviated month
        '%B': r'[A-Za-z]+',  # Full month
        '%c': r'.+',         # Locale's appropriate date and time representation
        '%x': r'.+',         # Locale's appropriate date representation
        '%X': r'.+',         # Locale's appropriate time representation
        '%%': r'%',          # Literal %
    }
    
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(format):
        if format[i] == '%' and i + 1 < len(format):
            code = format[i:i+2]
            if code in CODE_MAP:
                result.append(CODE_MAP[code])
                i += 2
            else:
                result.append(re.escape(code))
                i += 2
        else:
            result.append(re.escape(format[i]))
            i += 1
    
    return ''.join(result)
```
